country.evidence_source: [/page/9/Text/3] Interestingly, more than half of the Japanese youth (i.e., 56.9%) belonged to the moderate synthesis-moderate confusion trajectory. Meanwhile, a small number of youth (i.e., 3.2%) belonged to the high synthesis-high confusion trajectory. These results suggest that while about half of Japanese youth may experience "moderate" identity conflicts, only a small number of their peers feel strongly conflicted about their identity. Although many Japanese adolescents experience identity conflict as Erikson (1968) claimed, intensity of the conflict was found to be moderate rather than strong. These findings may reflect that the nature of valuing conformity in Japanese culture (Gordon, 2015) prevents Japanese youth from thoroughly facing strong identity conflicts.
